name: gnome

attributes.attribute: lived under the ground and worked as miners
not a Celtic creature and carries no folk legends

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The gnome is not a Celtic creature. It entered Celtic lands from medieval science and alchemy. Thinkers gave each element a being. Salamanders meant fire. Nereids meant water. Sylphs meant air. Gnomes meant earth. People thought gnomes lived under the ground and worked as miners. The word may come from genomus, which means earth-dweller. Gnomes have no folk legends. People confuse them with fairies and knockers. The dwarfs of Sleeping Beauty are a version of the gnome.

okr.objective: Frame the gnome as a medieval alchemy being distinct from native Celtic creatures.
key_results: The gnome came from medieval science and alchemy, not Celtic tradition.
Gnomes stood for the earth element among the four elements.
The word may derive from genomus, meaning earth-dweller.
